top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a falsifiable prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald flat bands at a magic angle, 2011) followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, since reproduced by many groups and extended across moire systems. A citation limited to flat bands and correlated phases does not depend on the unresolved pairing mechanism. The costs are real: the field is under a decade old, Cao and the first-author team fall outside three names, and Bistritzer takes the third place. P003 (Katori and Ye) is the cleaner, more mature and better-attributed fallback, so I rank it second. P002 ranks third because it pairs two unrelated achievements and rests B002 on a single name for a collaboration-scale discovery. No award is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for B028, B022 or B002; I direct WACQT and am at Chalmers, so I again note Chalmers institutional ties in superconducting circuits, which bear on B014 and not on any proposal in the slate
